name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis, including an in-driver taste-funnel explore state and design-ratification state) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (spec-build-driver.js stepped, driver-stepped: admission, wave derivation, gate resolution, red-check, the final gate, scope-reconcile, and the ledger row driven; test-author dispatch, per-wave worker dispatch, and repair held by the session) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, driver-stepped: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.52.0 — escape class contract (specs/20260901/07-escape-class-contract.md): every escape row now carries either a validated defect class or an explicit `unclassedReason` (`no-fix-diff`|`deferred`); `spec/scripts/lib/escape-row.js` is the one validator and `spec/scripts/escape-row.js` the one writer (`--check`, `--append` duplicate-refusing, `--amend`), retiring escape.md's `printf` append. A historical row's class is repaired by an append-only `stage:"escape-class"` amendment keyed by the original's `ts`+`spec`+`file`; latest amendment wins. `fleet-reader.js` counts recurrences on the joined (row + amendment) class, lists rows still needing a class as `escapes.unclassedRows`, and flags unvalidated rows in the drift census. `/spec:escape` classifies registry-first (fleet `byClass` keys plus the corpus's classes, before inventing a new id) and gains a one-time fleet-wide `--backfill` mode; `/spec:doctor` reports the backfill as due; core.md's Incident Policy Materiality bullet now cites the joined count. 7.51.0 — shell-composed mocks (specs/20260901/04-shell-composed-mocks.md): mocks now share one canonical app shell instead of each author copying chrome by hand — `design/shell/<name>.html` (plus a linked `.css`) is the canon, a page mock declares `data-shell="<name>"`/`"none"` and owns only its content slot, and `design-atlas.js shell sync` rewrites every declaring mock's region from canon byte-for-byte (active-nav derived, `built` mocks skipped by default); `shell adopt` migrates pre-shell mocks via a confirmed plan. `check` gains a tiered shell family (warn at `sketch`, violation at `ratified`/`approved`/`--matrix`); genesis `--mark tokens-landed` now also requires the shell canon to pass `check`, and `--mark rules-locked` authors `AppShell` from it. Sketch-tier authorship (the atlas gap sweep, sketch's scoped sweep) moves to the planning seat (ADR-0003, reversing specs/20260810/01 D8): the journey-central set in-session, the rest by one sequential `Agent {model: "fable"}` dispatch (Opus fallback), Sonnet mechanical-only, grounded in the picked position brief — restored to one shared paragraph in design.md § Design Atlas that atlas.md/sketch.md both cite, named in both commands' reports via a new `🎨 position: …` bullet. 7.50.0 — unified build loop (specs/20260901/03-unified-build-loop.md): /spec:build becomes the per-feature loop carrying a spec from hardened to done, deriving the next stage from disk and running design (when due), then the build driver, then the review driver in sequence, each `--via loop`. One checkpoint is enforced: a loop-driven review parks at a new CHECKPOINT state after the reviewer returns and refuses DISPOSITIONS until the session id in `.claude/spec-session.json` changes (a `/clear` and re-run), once per run, degrading to a printed warning when no stamp exists; the pre-merge stop stays the existing worktree step-out, never a forced clear. `spec-state-gate.sh` admits `/spec:build` on `hardened|implementing|done`. `core.md`'s § State Machine now attributes each transition to a driver state rather than a command: plan's lock → `hardened`, the build driver's preflight → `implementing`, the review driver's close → `done`; `/spec:build` runs both drivers in sequence and `/spec:review` remains the review driver's direct entry. `fleet-reader.js` gains the seventh fixed question `cleanByVia`, scoring escapes-per-CLEAN separately for `loop` / `direct` / `unknown` review rows — the number the brief's kill condition reads.
